question.problem:
What is the solution to the following system of inequalities?

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3t-2<-8 \\ t+1<-2\end{aligned}
$$

The solution is
$t$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $t$ that satisfy both $3t-2<-8$ and $t+1<-2$ simultaneously.

- First, we solve $3t-2<-8\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3t-2 & <-8 \\ 3t-2+2 & <-8+2 \\ 3t & <-6 \\ \frac{3t}{3} & <\frac{-6}{3} \\ t & <-2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/b97b78ec613e826f7f8beb7336d3c2f285fc58d9bbf0c0f9d59921f41de2b3b6.png)

$$

$$

- Then, we solve $t+1<-2\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}t+1 & <-2 \\ t+1-1 & <-2-1 \\ t & <-3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/cfb26921afb706908f771e1934cf27c0ca6e248e9e3aca54f499af685393fa86.png)

$$

$$

To find the values of $t$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/6d488376420476cf34798aeb3fced46770a177288b550f2e887348c582741321.png)

 

$$

$$

Thus, the final solution is $t<-3.$
